topicName: Reflection of Light and Curved Mirrors
description: A study of how light reflects from plane and curved mirrors, the laws of reflection, image formation, and the everyday uses of concave and convex mirrors.

mcq.questionText: What does the law of reflection state about the angle of incidence and the angle of reflection?

options.text: They are always equal to each other
The angle of incidence is always larger
The angle of reflection is always larger

mcq.explanation: The first law of reflection states that the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.

mcq.questionText: From which point on a reflecting surface are the angles of incidence and reflection measured?

options.text: From the normal at the point of incidence
From the edge of the mirror

mcq.explanation: Both angles are measured from the normal, which is the line drawn perpendicular to the surface at the point where the ray strikes.

mcq.questionText: Which type of reflection occurs when parallel rays strike a smooth, polished surface such as a plane mirror?
mcq.explanation: Regular reflection happens on smooth surfaces, where parallel incident rays remain parallel after reflection.

mcq.questionText: Why can you see your face in a smooth mirror but not on a rough wall painted the same colour?

options.text: The rough wall causes diffuse reflection, scattering rays in many directions
The wall does not reflect any light at all
The mirror does not obey the laws of reflection

mcq.explanation: A rough surface scatters reflected rays in many directions (diffuse reflection), so no clear image forms.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a property of an image formed by a plane mirror?

options.text: It is the same size as the object
It is always smaller than the object

mcq.explanation: A plane mirror image is virtual, upright, the same size as the object, and laterally inverted; it is never smaller.

mcq.questionText: An object is placed 8 cm in front of a plane mirror. How far is the image behind the mirror?
mcq.explanation: In a plane mirror the image distance behind the mirror equals the object distance in front, so the image is 8 cm behind.

mcq.questionText: What is the term for the point on the principal axis through which all rays parallel to the axis pass after reflection from a concave mirror?
mcq.explanation: The focal point (principal focus) is where rays parallel to the principal axis converge after reflection from a concave mirror.

mcq.questionText: Which mirror is also known as a converging mirror?
mcq.explanation: A concave mirror brings parallel rays together at a focus, so it is called a converging mirror.

mcq.questionText: What is the relationship between the radius of curvature (R) and the focal length (f) of a curved mirror?
mcq.explanation: For a curved mirror the radius of curvature is twice the focal length, so R = 2f.

mcq.questionText: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 30 cm. What is its focal length?
mcq.explanation: Since f = R/2, the focal length is 30/2 = 15 cm.

mcq.questionText: What kind of image does a convex mirror always form of a real object?

options.text: Real, upright and the same size

mcq.explanation: A convex (diverging) mirror always forms a virtual, upright and diminished image of a real object.

mcq.questionText: Why are convex mirrors used as driving (rear-view) and shop security mirrors?

options.text: They magnify objects so they look closer
They give a wide field of view
They form real images on a screen
They invert the image for safety

mcq.explanation: Convex mirrors diverge reflected rays, allowing a wider area to be seen in a small mirror.

mcq.questionText: Where must an object be placed in front of a concave mirror to produce a magnified, upright, virtual image (as in a shaving or make-up mirror)?

options.text: Between the focal point and the mirror

mcq.explanation: When the object is closer than the focal point, a concave mirror produces an enlarged, upright, virtual image.

mcq.questionText: An object is placed exactly at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. What is the nature of the image formed?

options.text: Real, inverted and the same size as the object, at the centre of curvature
Real, inverted and diminished at the focal point
Virtual, upright and the same size behind the mirror

mcq.explanation: With the object at C, the image is real, inverted, the same size as the object and also located at C.

mcq.questionText: Why is a concave reflector placed behind the bulb in a car headlamp or torch?

options.text: To scatter the light over a wide area
To absorb excess heat from the bulb
To reflect light into a strong parallel beam when the bulb is at the focus
To form a magnified image of the bulb

mcq.explanation: When the light source is at the focal point of a concave mirror, the reflected rays emerge parallel, giving a powerful beam.

fib.questionText: The line drawn perpendicular to a mirror at the point where a ray strikes is called the _____.
fib.explanation: Angles of incidence and reflection are always measured from the normal.

fib.questionText: Reflection from a rough or uneven surface that scatters light in many directions is called _____ reflection.
fib.explanation: Diffuse reflection occurs on rough surfaces and does not form a clear image.

fib.questionText: The image formed in a plane mirror is _____ inverted, meaning left and right appear swapped.
fib.explanation: Lateral inversion is why text appears reversed in a plane mirror.

fib.questionText: An image that cannot be caught on a screen because the rays only appear to meet is called a _____ image.
fib.explanation: Plane and convex mirrors form virtual images; concave mirrors can form real or virtual images.

fib.questionText: A mirror that curves inwards, like the inside of a spoon, is called a _____ mirror.
fib.explanation: A concave mirror has a reflecting surface that curves inward and converges light.

fib.questionText: A mirror that bulges outwards and diverges light is called a _____ mirror.
fib.explanation: A convex mirror spreads reflected rays apart and always forms small, upright virtual images.

fib.questionText: The centre of the sphere of which a curved mirror forms part is called the centre of _____.
fib.explanation: The centre of curvature (C) lies on the principal axis at a distance equal to the radius of curvature.

fib.questionText: The imaginary straight line passing through the pole and the centre of curvature of a curved mirror is the _____ axis.
fib.explanation: The principal axis is the main reference line for tracing rays in curved mirrors.

fib.questionText: The distance between the pole of a curved mirror and its focal point is called the _____ length.
fib.explanation: The focal length (f) equals half the radius of curvature.

fib.questionText: Because it makes a small mirror show a large area, the convex mirror is used as a _____ mirror in cars to see traffic behind.
fib.explanation: Convex mirrors give a wide field of view, useful for rear-view and security mirrors.

tf.questionText: The angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection.
tf.explanation: This is the first law of reflection and applies to all reflecting surfaces.

tf.questionText: The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane.
tf.explanation: This is the second law of reflection.

tf.questionText: A plane mirror produces a real image that can be formed on a screen.
tf.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual image, which cannot be captured on a screen.

tf.questionText: The image in a plane mirror is the same size as the object.
tf.explanation: Plane mirror images are upright, virtual, laterally inverted and of equal size to the object.

tf.questionText: A convex mirror can form a magnified real image of a distant object.
tf.explanation: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, upright and diminished image of a real object.

tf.questionText: A concave mirror can produce either a real or a virtual image depending on the object's position.
tf.explanation: A concave mirror gives a virtual image when the object is inside the focus and a real image otherwise.

tf.questionText: The focal length of a curved mirror is twice its radius of curvature.
tf.explanation: It is the opposite: the radius of curvature is twice the focal length, R = 2f.

tf.questionText: Diffuse reflection is the reason we can see objects that are not light sources from many angles.
tf.explanation: Rough surfaces scatter light in many directions, allowing us to see them from different positions.

tf.questionText: Convex mirrors are used in car headlamps to produce a strong parallel beam of light.
tf.explanation: Concave mirrors are used in headlamps; placing the bulb at the focus produces a parallel beam.

tf.questionText: When an object is placed at the focal point of a concave mirror, the reflected rays emerge parallel and no clear image is formed at a finite distance.
tf.explanation: Rays from an object at the focus reflect parallel, so the image is said to be formed at infinity.

summary.correctAnswer: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and the incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in one plane.
summary.explanation: These two laws govern how all light reflects from surfaces.

summary.correctAnswer: Smooth surfaces give regular reflection and clear images; rough surfaces give diffuse reflection and scattered light.
summary.explanation: Both still obey the laws of reflection at each point.

summary.questionText: Properties of a plane mirror image
summary.correctAnswer: Virtual, upright, same size as the object, laterally inverted, and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
summary.explanation: These four features describe every plane mirror image.

summary.correctAnswer: A converging mirror that curves inward and can form real or virtual images depending on object position.
summary.explanation: Used in shaving mirrors, headlamps and telescopes.

summary.correctAnswer: A diverging mirror that curves outward and always forms a virtual, upright, diminished image.
summary.explanation: Gives a wide field of view, used as rear-view and security mirrors.

summary.correctAnswer: The centre of the sphere of which the mirror is a part, lying on the principal axis at distance R.
summary.explanation: A ray through C strikes the mirror normally and reflects back on itself.

summary.correctAnswer: The point where rays parallel to the principal axis converge (or appear to diverge from) after reflection.
summary.explanation: It lies halfway between the pole and centre of curvature.

summary.correctAnswer: The straight line through the pole and the centre of curvature of a curved mirror.
summary.explanation: It is the reference line used for ray diagrams.

summary.correctAnswer: The radius of curvature is twice the focal length: R = 2f, so f = R/2.
summary.explanation: This lets you find one value from the other.

summary.correctAnswer: Concave mirrors are used in headlamps, torches and shaving mirrors; convex mirrors in rear-view and security mirrors.
summary.explanation: The choice depends on whether converging or a wide view is needed.

hoq.questionText: A concave mirror of focal length 10 cm is used to form an image of an object placed 30 cm in front of it. Using the mirror formula 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, what is the image distance?
hoq.explanation: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = 1/10 - 1/30 = 2/30, so v = 15 cm; the real image forms 15 cm in front of the mirror.

hoq.questionText: A 4 cm tall object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror of focal length 12 cm. What is the height and nature of the image?
hoq.explanation: At the centre of curvature (R = 2f = 24 cm) the magnification is 1, so the image is the same size (4 cm), real and inverted.
